fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Smooth cut stone in wide horizontal courses — large flat ashlar blocks, cool grey, nothing on the face. You would put a hand on something flat and dry with a joint every 25–30 px and nothing between the joints.
fields.Q1_WHY:
At 1:1 I cannot tell at all — the whole standing region sits at luma 8–17 out of 255 and reads as black. The material only appears under a ~20× contrast stretch. Stretched, `x 80–400, y 0–200` shows three clean horizontal courses (~65 px tall) with staggered vertical joints ~55 px apart. `x 0–55, y 220–470` shows the same wide horizontal banding. A 100×50 px patch of it at `x 0–50, y 300–400` contains **15 unique RGB values**; the interior floor at `x 300–400, y 300–400` contains **432**.

The one place the wall material is genuinely lit is the isolated block at `x 183–250, y 393–462` — same coursing, mean luma 66. That is what I'm naming from.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
**Flat pattern.** And I can prove it rather than assert it.

The block at `x 183–250, y 393–462` stands inside the room, 200 px west of the lamp. I normalised the image by its own azimuthal median radial falloff around the light at ~`(412, 430)` and sampled due west: at r=170/200/230 (through the block) normalised luma is 0.27 / 0.26 / 0.33. At **r=260 — immediately past it — the value is 1.11.** Full brightness, instantly. That block occludes nothing. A solid standing object in a point-lit room throws no shadow at all.

Second tell: the boundary line. It is exactly 4 px (`y 171–174`) at every x I sampled from 60 to 680, and its value is **2–5 regardless of local exposure** while the floor beside it ranges 9 → 24. A contact shadow scales with the light. A constant does not. That is a drawn outline.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
North edge: `y = 171`, dead flat across the entire width `x 60 → 680`, no jog, no offset, no broken course anywhere. South edge: `y = 713`, equally flat `x 60 → 680`. West edge: `x = 55`. **There is no east edge in frame** — at `x 640–750, y 300–640` the floor's hatched block pattern runs continuously off the right side of the screen.

Across the north transition, at `x = 320`: `15 15 16 16 17 17 | 4 4 4 4 | 8 8 8 8 9 9`. **Four pixels.** Floor value → flat black → wall value. No bevel, no cap highlight, no dither, no gradient. The south seam is marginally better — the floor blocks meet it with a ragged 1 px dither around `y 690–713` — but the wall's own line below it is again dead straight.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.**

There is exactly one made object anywhere on the standing structure: a vertical bar with three horizontal rungs at `x 133–143, y 130–170` — about 10×40 px, a driven pin or a short ladder. It sits in the middle of a wall course. It does not span a joint, does not bridge a break, does not cross the corner it sits beside. It is holding nothing. It is also at luma 10–21, meaning it is invisible on the screen; I found it under a contrast stretch.

Nothing else. No rope, no strap, no timber, no bracket, no pin, no shoring, in 750×800 pixels.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**
**Repeated** — though not in the way that word usually means, so let me be precise, because the obvious version of the charge is false.

Autocorrelation across the north wall (`y 5–165, x 90–430`) and the west wall (`y 230–700, x 2–52`) shows monotone decay in both axes out to lag 120 — **no periodic peak, no literal tiling.** The block layout is genuinely varied.

But look at the top-left corner, `x 0–140, y 110–250`. The wall's horizontal courses run straight *through* the corner without interruption — the same course lines continue from the north band into the west band as one uninterrupted horizontal field. No quoin, no toothing, no change of direction. The west wall's courses run perpendicular to the wall's own length. This is one flat texture field with a 635×542 rectangle punched out of it. Nothing in it is a consequence of anything else standing up.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**
YES — it would pass unremarked in a mid-tier roguelike.

Merely competent, or genuinely good? **Merely competent.** The competence is real and it is all in the floor, which I have been told not to discuss. The standing structure is a black band with a 4 px outline.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?**
Legible at 1:1, without magnifying:
- The block at `x 183–250, y 393–462` — its hard black top/left outline, two courses, four or five flat rectangles inside.
- A row of dark rectangles along `y 175–205`, roughly `x 200–560`, brightest either side of the corridor mouth.
- The corridor as a warmer column above the room.

That is the complete list. Everything else is black.

Not legible at 1:1 — only after magnification and heavy contrast stretch: the coursing of the west wall, the south wall, and all four corners; the pin at `x 133–143, y 130–170`; every joint below `y 205`; the entire right-hand side.

Distance dependence, yes, and it is severe: azimuthal median luma around the lamp falls 114.9 at r=60 → 33.4 at r=220 → **16.5 at r=260**. Past ~250 px from the figure the standing surface is under luma 20 and is black on a phone. Since the figure sits at `(412, 430)` and the walls sit at 55, 171 and 713, **most of the wall in this image is past that radius.** The one wall surface that *is* well-lit — that block, mean luma 66 — is blank: high-frequency energy normalised by brightness is **0.065**, against **0.089** for floor at comparable exposure. The best-lit piece of standing stone in the frame carries less surface incident than the ground it stands on.
fields.Q8:
IS THERE ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Three things, and the third is the one that matters.

1. The 4 px black line. Same width, same value 2–5, north seam `y 171–174` and around the standing block at `x 183–250, y 393–462`. The block's outline is the perimeter's outline reused at object scale.
2. The absolute straightness. `y=171` for 620 px; `y=713` for 620 px. Every sample lands on the same row.
3. **The courses run horizontally on all three walls in frame.** North (`y 0–170`), west (`x 0–55`), south (`y 715–790`) — all wide horizontal bands with vertical joints. On the west wall, that is coursing running across the wall instead of along it. It is one texture in one orientation stamped over every wall regardless of which way the wall runs.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
It is a **surface, at the same height, in a different stone** — not mass, not void, not another room.

What told me: it takes the lamp's light on its face. At `x = 300` the region beyond the seam brightens from luma 9 at `y=100` to **21 at `y=170`**, rising toward the room. It is lit by the same falloff that lights the floor, and at the north seam it is *brighter* than the floor immediately inside it (21 above the line, 15 below). Something with mass would either present a cap and a shadow, or fall to nothing. This presents neither. It behaves like more ground in a smoother stone.

At 1:1 none of that is available. On screen it is black, and black reads as void by default — so the picture says one thing and the pixels say another.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END?**
Found it: `x 376 → 437`, running north from `y=171` off the top of the frame. The seam scan confirms it — `y=171` is continuous at every x except 380–420.

I read it as **a passage** — but entirely on the light, not the structure. Lamplight spills up it: `(400, 100)` is luma ~34 against the flanking wall at ~4. That is the only cue. Structurally there is nothing: the coursing is cut off at a straight vertical line with no jamb, no return face, no wall-end, no lintel. Cover the light spill and this is indistinguishable from a notch. On a dead end — where by definition no light escapes — you would have nothing to go on.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
No. Nothing has happened to it.

Read from: a north edge that holds `y=171` across 620 px and a south edge that holds `y=713` across 620 px without a single deviation; no breach, no collapse, no bulge, no missing block, no patch, no fallen debris banked at any base, no soot, no staining, no repair. One 10×40 px pin at `x 133–143, y 130–170`, holding nothing, invisible on screen.

Four hundred years of a company that repairs with rope and driven pins, in a place nobody has ever cared for, and the wall line is machine-straight for 542 pixels. This structure has no history.

---

- Give the standing stone a cap face and a cast shadow: the block at `x 183–250, y 393–462` must throw a shadow west; right now normalised luma past it returns to 1.11 immediately.
- Replace the constant 4 px black seam at `y=171` / `y=713` / `x=55` with a lit edge that varies with the lamp — bright cap where light strikes, contact shadow that scales.

- Raise the wall's ambient floor so the material is above black at `x 0–55` and `y 715–790`; and put real incident on the face — the lit block at `(183–250, 393–462)` currently carries less detail per unit brightness than the floor (0.065 vs 0.089).
